did_you_know.text: The word “sneh” probably describes a thorny bush, but we do not know exactly which species it was. The wonder is that the bush burns without being consumed.
Removing one’s shoes can express respect and awe in a holy place. Even today, people remove their shoes before entering some sacred spaces.
“Pharaoh” was not the Egyptian king’s personal name, but a title meaning “the great house,” referring to the royal palace. Later, the title came to refer to the king himself.

The phrase “Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh” is related to the verb “to be” and can also be translated as “I will be what I will be” or “I am who I am.” Its wording preserves mystery rather than reducing God to one definition.
The name YHWH is written with four letters, so it is called the “Tetragrammaton.” In Jewish tradition, it is generally read as “Adonai” rather than pronounced as written.
“A land flowing with milk and honey” is a vivid expression for a fertile, abundant land. The milk suggests rich pastures and livestock, while the honey may refer mainly to date syrup or bee honey.
In the ancient world, metal objects and clothing were valuable possessions that could be carried easily. The Israelites’ departure is therefore described as leaving with property, not empty-handed.
